assessment_summary: The statement is false. A counterexample is a bipartite graph where A has 2 vertices, B has 1 vertex, and both vertices of A are connected to the single vertex of B. In this graph, every vertex of A has degree 1 (which is at least 1), and every vertex of B has degree 2 (which is at most 2). However, a maximum matching can contain at most 1 edge since |B|=1, so it cannot saturate A.
counterexample:
Let G be a bipartite graph with parts A = {a1, a2} and B = {b1}. Let the edges of G be {a1, b1} and {a2, b1}. 
Then every vertex of A has degree 1 (≥ 1), and every vertex of B has degree 2 (≤ 2). 
However, the maximum matching in G has size min(|A|, |B|) = 1, so no matching can saturate all 2 vertices of A.
